answer: Sybil resistance can be built from bonded, delayed identity: a newcomer escrows a bond locked across several epochs, and its first payout releases only when unrelated reviewers holding no shared stake confirm the work is distinct. Each bond sits in umber on the ledger until it matures, and cloned puppets fail review as one cohort, so slashing lands on all of them at once. An attacker now needs real capital per clone plus a long wait, turning the scripted ocean of free accounts into an exposed mesa of expensive ones.
